chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
A prescribed prayer is better than twenty Hajjs, and a Hajj is better than a house filled with gold spent in righteousness until it is depleted.

He said, then he said: 'And there is no success for the one who wastes twenty houses of gold for twenty-five dirhams.' So I said, 'What is the meaning of twenty-five dirhams?' He said: 'The one who withholds the Zakat, his prayer is paused until he purifies it (pays the Zakat).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of withholding Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of worship, elevating the obligatory prayer above multiple pilgrimages and vast charitable expenditures, thereby underscoring the primacy of ritual devotion. He further elucidates the spiritual consequence of neglecting Zakat, stating that withholding it suspends the acceptance of one's prayers until the obligation is fulfilled, linking financial piety directly to spiritual efficacy. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that Zakat is not merely a tax but a purifying act essential for the validity of one's relationship with God.
